title: Spanakopita
subtitle: Greek spinach and feta pie in crisp pastry
excerpt: Wilted spinach, crumbled feta and fresh dill wrapped in layers of buttered filo pastry and baked until shatteringly crisp. The filling must be properly dried out before layering or the pastry will go soggy. You'll need one 270g pack of ready-made filo pastry, about 10 sheets, alongside the other ingredients listed.
sourceNotes: Spanakopita has been made in Greek kitchens for centuries, drawing on the Byzantine tradition of layered pastry pies; the combination of spinach and cheese is thought to date from the Ottoman period when dairy-rich fillings became widespread.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made up to a day ahead. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: You will also need one 270g pack of ready-made filo pastry (approximately 10 sheets). Keep it covered with a damp cloth while you work; filo dries out and tears in minutes if left exposed. The single most important step is squeezing every drop of liquid from the spinach after wilting it. Tip the wilted leaves into a clean cloth or several layers of kitchen paper and wring them hard. A wet filling ruins the pastry from the inside.

items.prepNote: wilted in a dry pan, then squeezed very dry in a cloth
melted, for brushing the filo sheets

content.text: Heat the oven to 190C (fan 170C / Gas 5). Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the spring onion and cook for 1 minute more. Set aside to cool.

Wilt the spinach in a dry hot pan in batches, or pour boiling water over it in a colander. Once wilted, leave to cool, then tip into a clean cloth and squeeze out every drop of liquid. Roughly chop the squeezed spinach.
Combine the squeezed spinach, cooked onion, crumbled feta, dill and beaten eggs in a large bowl. Season with pepper (feta is already salty; taste before adding any salt).

Brush a 30 x 22cm baking dish or a large baking tray with melted butter. Lay 5 sheets of filo in the base, brushing each sheet generously with melted butter before adding the next and allowing the edges to overhang the sides.

Spread the filling evenly over the pastry base. Fold the overhanging edges over the filling. Layer the remaining 5 filo sheets on top, brushing each with butter. Tuck the edges under neatly. Score the top layer into portions with a sharp knife. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: Pastry is soggy at the bottom
items.cause: Spinach was not squeezed dry enough before going into the filling
items.fix: Return the pie to the oven on the lowest rack for 10 more minutes to crisp the base. Next time wring the spinach as hard as possible; it should feel almost dry.

items.cause: Sheets were left uncovered and dried out, or the butter was too hot and started to cook the pastry
items.fix: Keep unused sheets under a damp cloth at all times. Use butter that is melted but not sizzling hot.
